error = float(np.linalg.norm(Operator(approx).data - qft_matrix(5), ord=2))

display(approx.draw(output="mpl", fold=32)); plt.close("all")

The notebook compares a five-wire truncated circuit with an independent Fourier matrix and checks its spectral error against the formula. Dedicated tests cover every cutoff for one through five wires, while exact circuits through six wires match the defining matrix. Dense matrix checks stop at eight wires. No integrated Lean proof or per-angle synthesis certificate is supplied.

The exact rational confidence allocation charges omission as a single-trial output-TV loss, separately from synthesis and whole-run physical faults.

Omission does not change the declared numerical phase tolerance. Its uniform distribution bound increases repetitions. The 24 bounded queries return 123 Pareto points. Omitting one gate saves five primitive operations per trial, but the conservative confidence contract increases repetitions from 15 to 127, 35 or 21. At each case’s fastest returned point, truncated/exact total serial-runtime ratios range from about
. This grid therefore shows no total-runtime improvement under its declared omission/inference policy.

children.value: Observed output-TV losses at phase 0.3 are much smaller than the uniform bounds: approximately 0.00907, 0.00343 and 0.000463. Omission slightly improves this selected phase’s good-output mass at seven bits. These diagnostics do not choose the repetition policy. A sharper independently established application-specific omission or inference contract could change the comparison; no such improvement is validated here.

All Pareto points, code distances, factory choices, canonical counts and QASM/source hashes are retained. Peak qubits times total runtime is a rectangular space-time proxy. The QDK mean synthesis fit supplies no worst-case per-angle approximation or runtime-tail certificate. Physical initialization/reset, external loading and classical median/controller/decoder/verification latency are excluded. The existing Grover baseline remains unchanged.

They use pinned Qiskit core 2.6.2, NumPy 2.5.4, Matplotlib 3.11.2 and the audited QDK 1.34.0 adapter; source snapshots and the MIT implementation license accompany the reports. Existing approximate-QFT and QPE references apply. No Lean proof or certified hardware implementation is integrated.
